subject: Request: Regional dedicated trial extension — hourly capacity vs credits
messages:
From: Sienna Park <sienna@brightedge.ai>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
Cc: BrightEdge Procurement <procurement@brightedge.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: extension + hourly dedicated capacity option

Hi Diego,

Thanks for the demo last week — team was impressed with the latency on short-context inference. We ran the POC for our search-rewrite flow and ended up using more dedicated tokens than we expected in week two (peak embed + generation workloads). I've attached a small usage extract so you can see the burst pattern.

We have two asks from the product and procurement teams:
- Can Redwood extend the POC by three weeks while we finish integration tests?
- Alternatively, can we convert the remaining trial credits into an hourly dedicated capacity pool (us-west1) for the remainder of the quarter? Procurement prefers an hourly/consumption model if possible.

If there are pricing examples or a short amendment we can sign, that would help speed approvals. We can be flexible on the exact size of the pool (start small, autoscale up), but need visibility on the all-in rate (tokens/hour or $/GPU-hour + token overage).

Attached: BrightEdge-usage-report-20260228.csv

Thanks,
Sienna Park
Head of ML Platform
BrightEdge AI

From: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
To: Sienna Park <sienna@brightedge.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: extension + hourly dedicated capacity option

Hi Sienna — thanks for the note and the usage file. High level: both options are feasible, but they have different operational and pricing implications.

Quick summary of options we can offer (draft numbers — will confirm with finance/legal):
1) 3-week POC extension + token credit: we can extend the hosted trial window by 21 days and top up ~150k token-equivalent credit to cover expected burst traffic. No infra changes needed; simplest path.

2) Hourly dedicated capacity (us-west1) conversion: convert remaining credits into a small dedicated GPU pool (we suggest starting with 1xA10 equivalent slot with autoscale to 2 for peaks). Pricing direction: $/GPU-hour + a reduced per-token overage (since batch execution lowers unit cost). I'll loop in Marcus for exact numbers.

Tradeoffs to note: the dedicated pool gives better predictability for heavy bursts and isolation, but requires a short amendment (region pin, hours cap, and billing cadence). The extension + token credit is fastest to approve but keeps you on shared-hosted runtime (no isolation).

Laura — can you confirm technical feasibility (A10 vs A100, autoscale behavior for short spikes) and estimate the minimum commitable hours for a small pool in us-west1?

Marcus — can you draft two price sketches (extension credit & hourly dedicated), including the discount tiers for a short-term conversion?

Sienna — if procurement wants a quick doc to circulate, I can prepare a 1-page amendment + estimated invoice.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai, Sienna Park <sienna@brightedge.ai>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 6 Mar 2026 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: extension + hourly dedicated capacity option

Diego / Sienna — quick engineering note:

- us-west1 supports both A10 and A100 pools. For short-burst, A10-equivalent with autoscale to 2 nodes is the most cost-efficient and matches your latency profile in the POC.
- Minimum allocatable block for dedicated pools is 10 GPU-hours for a 24-hour billing window (we bill by the hour but require a minimum top-up to create the pool).
- We can enable prefix/KV caching to reduce token charges for repeated queries; that will change token burn in the attached usage report.

If you choose the conversion to dedicated hours we will:
1) Provision the pool in us-west1 and pin to your org for the requested window.
2) Provide a daily usage report and a rolling 24-hour peak metric so you have alerting.
3) Offer a one-time configuration assistance session (1-2 hours) to tune batching & caching.

Attaching a proposed ratecard for dedicated GPU-hours (draft): proposed-ratecard-dedicated-hours-2026-03-10.pdf

Let me know if you want me to include estimated cost for enabling AVX-optimized kernels vs default; that can shave costs for heavy generation.

—Laura
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, Sienna Park <sienna@brightedge.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: extension + hourly dedicated capacity option

Diego / Laura / Sienna — pricing sketches below (numbers are round, include a short-term conversion discount for POC customers). Please consider these internal drafts until legal approves an amendment.

Option A — 3-week extension + token credit
- 150,000 token-equivalent credit top-up
- No infra change; billed only if credit is exceeded at published hosted rates
- No change to SLA or isolation
- Effective price impact: ~ $9k gross (to show in invoice as credit applied)

Option B — Hourly dedicated capacity (conversion of remaining credits)
- Minimum pool: 10 GPU-hours to create the pool (billed at creation)
- Suggested base configuration: 1xA10-equivalent with autoscale to 2 (start/peak)
- Ratecard (draft): $6.00 / GPU-hour base, 10% discount for this short conversion, added per-token overage at $0.00008 / token for generation after caching savings
- Example for three weeks with modest burst: ~ 250 GPU-hours => list ~$1,350; with discount ~$1,215 + expected token overage (estimate $2k) => ~$3,215

Notes:
- The dedicated option reduces per-token unit cost; however, if utilization is very low the extension + credit path is likely cheaper.
- We can include a one-time 15% goodwill discount if BrightEdge signs the short amendment this week (internal approval needed from sales leader).

Lauren (legal) — please prepare a short amendment template that:
1) Pins region (us-west1) and pool size / scaling rules.
2) Converts remaining credit into prepaid GPU-hours or bills hourly (we need to clarify billing cadence).

Sienna — if you prefer, we can present both options to procurement with line items so they can choose.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Finance Operations, Redwood Inference

From: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
To: Sienna Park <sienna@brightedge.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 17:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: extension + hourly dedicated capacity option

Sienna — following up with a concrete path so procurement can move quickly.

Choice and next steps (pick A or B):
A) Extension route (fastest)
- Redwood issues a 21-day extension and applies 150k token credit.
- No amendment required; we will send an invoice reflecting the credit for internal accounting.
- Target: sign-off via email by EOD Thu 3/12.

B) Dedicated-hour conversion (recommended if you expect repeated bursts)
- We will convert the remaining credit to an initial prepay of 100 GPU-hours in us-west1 (creates the pool + 24h billing window).
- Draft amendment to pin region and autoscale policy attached; Lauren will send DocuSign.
- Pricing example (after the 10% conversion discount and Marcus' goodwill 15% if approved): estimated first-run cost ~$2,700 including token overage buffer.

If procurement wants a line-item doc, I've attached a 1-page amendment + the proposed ratecard. Lauren: please prepare DocuSign that includes the pool config and the billing cadence (prepay vs hourly invoice).

Evelyn — can you prepare a 30-minute handoff call script and a proposed tuning slot (we recommend 60–90 mins of SE time) to align on batching and cache keys after provisioning?

Sienna — what do you prefer? Reply with A or B and we'll get the paperwork moving.

Cheers,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
